title: bug: Restart Daemon kills whatever pid a repository-supplied .moe/daemon.json names
description: MoeProjectService.restartDaemon reads .moe/daemon.json and calls ProcessHandle.of(info.pid).destroy() whenever that pid is alive, with no provenance check. readDaemonInfo also skips its project-path check when projectPath is empty. A repository can commit .moe/daemon.json naming any pid the user may signal, and the Restart Daemon button then kills that process. Under the protected profile, gate the kill on RuntimeSelectionPolicy.verifyProvenance, or kill only the supervisor's own spawned process. Found by CQ-R01 (task-3b760109c42544ab892199b3d5534b77), whose plan scopes MoeProjectService to the doConnect/connect gates.
definitionOfDone: Under the protected profile, Restart Daemon never signals a process whose provenance RuntimeSelectionPolicy.verifyProvenance does not confirm
Legacy Restart Daemon behavior is unchanged, or the change is explicitly decided and tested

implementationPlan.description: Add restart regressions to RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest using its existing service/project/status fixtures and a proposed injected supervisor ProcessHandle resolver returning inert spy handles. Cover PROTECTED unrecorded PID, stale start/PID reuse, another project's record, empty daemon.json projectPath, missing start information and malformed-profile fail-closed selection: zero destroy calls. Cover a recorded supervisor/direct child allowed exactly once, dead/absent process allowing stale metadata cleanup, and LEGACY unrecorded live PID preserving its prior signal/cleanup/reconnect semantics. Exercise real service.restartDaemon on refusal: metadata bytes preserved, refusal status visible, no new process start or retry/backoff reset. Test resolver/signal exceptions and destroy=false under protected vs legacy; never call destroy on the test JVM or any external process.
implementationPlan.note:
Added restart regressions R1-R4 to RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest (+172/-3). They drive the real service.restartDaemon() through a reflection-injected supervisor (the same pattern G4 uses) whose new processLookup returns inert SignalSpy proxies. destroy is only recorded and never reaches a process.
- R1 PROTECTED refusals, zero destroys: unrecorded, pid reused (stale start), another project's record, spawn without a start instant, blank daemon.json projectPath, unreadable project.json (real profile).
- R2: LEGACY unrecorded live pid signaled once and restarted. PROTECTED recorded supervisor and its direct child (a real `sort` child, spy-signaled) each stopped exactly once.
- R3: dead, vanished, and pid 0/-1 under both profiles: no lookup, no signal, stale daemon.json removed, restart goes on.
- R4: lookup throws, destroy throws, destroy=false. PROTECTED refuses, LEGACY continues.
A refusal asserts daemon.json bytes kept, nothing started, statuses exactly [Disconnected, refusal], spawn attempts untouched (preset to Int.MAX_VALUE), no reconnect timer.
Tests pin the restart-refusal text. supervisorFor gained trailing alive/lookup params (defaults unchanged for existing tests).
RED: these reference the step-2 supervisor parameter, so they compile only after step 2. The meaningful RED run (supervisor API present, service not yet wired) is done in step 2.
Every test pid is the test JVM's own (the JDK refuses to destroy the current process), its own `sort` child, or 0/-1, so even the pre-fix path cannot signal an external process.

implementationPlan.description: Move only the restart PID-signal operation into a small supervisor method (proposed stopDaemonForRestart(info): String?, null = may continue, string = refusal). Add an optional trailing ProcessHandle lookup constructor dependency defaulting to ProcessHandle.of(pid).orElse(null), consistent with current probes. Preserve the existing live/dead decision; capture a live target handle once, require activationRefusal(info)==null under the protected profile immediately before signaling, then destroy that captured handle rather than resolving the PID again. Missing/dead handle is no signal. Under PROTECTED a provenance refusal or lookup/signal error/false destroy fails closed with a bounded actionable reason; error handling must not fall through to cleanup or reconnect. LEGACY keeps the old best-effort signal behavior, including continuing after signal failure. Do not use argv, repo metadata ownership claims, killSpawnedDaemon fallback or a new trust mechanism. Keep a short why-comment explaining repository metadata is not authority.
implementationPlan.note:
MoeDaemonSupervisor: added a trailing constructor dependency, processLookup: (Long) -> ProcessHandle? = { ProcessHandle.of(it).orElse(null) }, and stopDaemonForRestart(info): String? (null = continue, string = refusal), +33 lines.
Order of the method:
1. The existing liveness decision (isProcessAlive), plus a non-positive pid guard.
2. Read the profile once.
3. Capture the handle once.
4. Under PROTECTED, require activationRefusal(info) == null (that is, RuntimeSelectionPolicy.verifyProvenance) right before signaling.
5. destroy() the captured handle, never re-resolving the pid. The JDK handle carries its start time, so a process that took over the pid is never signaled.
Fail-closed handling under PROTECTED: a null handle means no signal (continue). Provenance refusal, a lookup or destroy exception, or destroy()==false return a bounded refusal (pid plus fixed text, never exception text). The text never calls the process a Moe daemon and says to identify/stop it yourself, then Restart Daemon.
LEGACY: best-effort destroy, exceptions swallowed (now logged), always continues. Same as before.
Explicit legacy decision, tested in R3: pid <= 0 is never looked up or signaled under either profile. An absent pid deserializes to 0, and kill(2) treats 0/-1 as process groups (the JDK would signal the IDE's own group on macOS for pid 0). On Windows/Linux, ProcessHandle.of(0/-1) is already empty, so behavior there is unchanged.
No argv, no killSpawnedDaemon fallback, no new trust mechanism.
RED run (focused, under the jetbrains-gradle lease): `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 cmd.exe /d /c "set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& gradlew.bat test --rerun --tests com.moe.util.RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest"` exit 1. 29 tests, 4 failed (R1-R4), 0 errors. Each failed for the right reason, because the service is not yet wired:
- R1: unrecorded protected pid, daemon.json deleted (expected kept).
- R4: protected lookup-throws restart proceeded.
- R2/R3: the old service ignores the supervisor lookup (spy never asked).

implementationPlan.description: Route restartDaemon through that supervisor stop method and remove its direct ProcessHandle.destroy path. After existing disconnect, if a stop refusal is returned, publishStatus(false, reason) and return before deleting daemon.json, resetting spawn/reconnect state or calling connect. Otherwise retain current stale-file deletion/backoff/reconnect flow. Missing or malformed metadata must never supply a signal target; preserve readDaemonInfo compatibility rather than changing global discovery rules. Keep UI guidance clear that an unverified process must be independently identified/stopped; no claim that a PID read from the repo is the daemon. Extend the tests from step 1 to pin the real service wiring and allowed branch; no test-only alternate restart implementation.
implementationPlan.note:
MoeProjectService.restartDaemon now routes through daemonSupervisor.stopDaemonForRestart(info) (+5/-5). The direct ProcessHandle.of(pid).destroy() path is gone, so the service has no ProcessHandle signal site left.
On refusal, after the existing disconnect(), it calls log.warn and publishStatus(false, reason), then returns. It returns before deleting daemon.json, resetSpawnBackoff, the reconnectAttempts reset and connect(). Otherwise the stale-file deletion, backoff reset and reconnect flow is unchanged.
readDaemonInfo is unchanged (global discovery compatibility kept). A blank projectPath still reads, but provenance decides (R1 row). Missing or malformed metadata never supplies a target: unreadable or absent daemon.json gives null, and pid<=0 gives no lookup.
Tests: SignalSpy now also records lookups. R2 asserts exactly one lookup and one destroy per allowed restart, pinning that the checked handle is the destroyed handle. R3 uses the spy's lookup record.
All tests go through the real service.restartDaemon wiring. There is no test-only restart implementation.

Traced and confirmed:
- Forged metadata cannot authorize a protected kill. A blank projectPath reads but provenance is keyed to this project's basePath, never info.projectPath (R1). A mismatched projectPath is deleted by discovery and never signaled. Missing or malformed JSON, or a missing projectPath (Gson null, NPE caught), returns null. An absent pid reads as 0 and is guarded. A non-int pid is a Gson error and returns null.
- PID, start and project identity come from the existing verifyProvenance (unrecorded, stale-start, other-project and no-start rows in R1).
- The captured handle is the destroyed handle, one lookup (R2; mutant M2 killed).
- Failed or false signals refuse before cleanup (R4; M1, M4, M6 killed). An Error from lookup/destroy unwinds out of restartDaemon before any cleanup.
- Legacy is unchanged except the explicit, tested pid<=0 guard plus a warn log (R2/R3/R4).
- No test reaches the default lookup. Pids used are the JVM's own, its `sort` child, or 0/-1.
- The service tests drive the production restartDaemon and supervisor method.
Theoretical, left as is:
(a) verifyProvenance reads fresh facts by pid. A reuse between capture and check is caught by the JDK start-time check on destroy (false, so PROTECTED refuses). Unknown start times also fail provenance.
(b) Two concurrent restarts: the second can briefly publish "the stop request failed" after the first stopped the daemon; fail-closed and transient.
(c) A recorded daemon exiting between lookup and check gets the "did not start it" refusal; a retry proceeds.
(d) Pre-existing: restart kills only the `_run` pid, not a live `start` supervisor (same as legacy; CQ-R13 owns restart atomicity and port binding).

comments.content: From CQ-R01 (task-3b760109c42544ab892199b3d5534b77) step-8 review: under the protected profile the activation refusal tells the user "Stop it, then use Restart Daemon." (RuntimeSelectionPolicy.verifyProvenance refusal text). Once the user has stopped that daemon, the pid in the repository-supplied .moe/daemon.json is dead or reused, so following the advice is exactly the path where restartDaemon kills an unrelated process. Fixing this bug should make restartDaemon verify the pid (e.g. RuntimeSelectionPolicy.verifyProvenance / a recorded spawn under PROTECTED, start instant + command under legacy) before destroying it; the refusal text can stay as is.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Reuse the landed RuntimeSelectionPolicy provenance via MoeDaemonSupervisor.activationRefusal; do not add another trust registry or infer ownership from daemon.json/argv. Preserve LEGACY behavior as the task permits; protect PROTECTED restart and surface refusal. Encapsulate only the existing PID-signal operation in the supervisor so tests can safely inject a ProcessHandle resolver. Three files, no schema/wire changes; CQ-R13 retains broader recovery/provenance work.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: restartDaemon currently disconnects, reads repo metadata, checks isProcessAlive, destroys ProcessHandle.of(pid), deletes metadata, resets backoff and connects. activationRefusal already calls verifyProvenance only under PROTECTED; its per-project pid/start records reject reused/unowned processes. RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest has real service/fake Project/status fixtures and supervisor injection, plus current-process provenance tests. Existing supplier constructor seam patterns in MoeDaemonSupervisor make safe spy handles possible without ever killing a real process.
planningNotes.risks: Security boundary: refusal must return BEFORE metadata removal, reset/reconnect or any signal fallback. Capture target handle once before provenance check and destroy that handle, never resolve a new pid afterward. Liveness is not provenance. No source/config mutation or arbitrary PID termination in tests. Empty projectPath must not bypass provenance. No unsupported auto-replacement or stronger isolation claim. Preserve legacy swallowed-signal-error behavior deliberately. Windows processes use parent/supervisor provenance, not unavailable argv.

completionSummary:
Under the protected profile, Restart Daemon no longer signals a pid from a repository-supplied .moe/daemon.json without provenance.
- MoeDaemonSupervisor: added stopDaemonForRestart(info): String? (null = continue, text = refusal) and a trailing processLookup (default ProcessHandle.of(pid).orElse(null)). Order: liveness, one profile read, capture the handle once. Under PROTECTED it requires activationRefusal(info)==null (verifyProvenance: per-project pid+start or a recorded supervisor parent), then destroys the captured handle, never re-resolved. PROTECTED fails closed on a provenance refusal, a lookup/destroy exception, or destroy()==false. The message is bounded: pid plus fixed text, never calls the process a Moe daemon, and says to identify and stop it, then Restart Daemon. LEGACY: best-effort destroy; errors are swallowed (now logged) and the restart continues.
- Decided legacy change, tested in R3: pid<=0 is never looked up or signaled in either profile. An absent pid reads as 0, and kill(2) treats 0/-1 as process groups. On Windows/Linux ProcessHandle.of(0/-1) is already empty, so nothing changes there.
- MoeProjectService.restartDaemon uses it. A refusal is logged and published, then it returns before deleting daemon.json, resetting backoff or connecting. readDaemonInfo is unchanged.
Tests (R1-R4 in RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest) drive the real restartDaemon with inert spy handles:
- R1 protected refusals: unrecorded, stale start, other project, no start instant, blank projectPath, unreadable project.json. Each has 0 signals, daemon.json bytes kept, no start, no backoff reset, no retry.
- R2: legacy, and a recorded supervisor and its child, each stopped once with one lookup.
- R3: dead, vanished, 0, -1.
- R4: lookup/destroy failures.
RED was 4/29 failing before wiring; mutation probes killed 9/9.
Filed: task-4f1e37f30ee548298b26e17c0b6ea84e (LOW): the daemon.json read has no size cap.
Not certified: OS-atomic restart and port binding (CQ-R13).
